notes: HOTFIX UI: PHF HR login hero (logo + system badge + title + subtitle) had no shared container - they were two independent flex children of .phf-test-login-brand, so on mobile the stacked logo/badge cluster (@media max-width:480px forced align-items:flex-start) sat flush-left while the title/subtitle text block spanned the full column width, reading as off-center/unbalanced. Added one minimal wrapper, .phf-login-hero (assets/js/phf-server-auth.js showLogin() template - the title/subtitle div had no class to hook, so a wrapper was required), around the existing .phf-login-logo-line and title/subtitle div, with no other DOM change. In index.html's login <style> block: .phf-login-hero replicates the exact flex-column/gap:26px .phf-test-login-brand previously used directly (desktop unchanged - brand now has a single child, hero absorbs the layout), and within the existing @media(max-width:860px) rule gets gap:18px + max-width:340px + margin:0 auto so logo/badge and title/description now share one centered reference width; .phf-login-logo-line got justify-content:center (860px rule, row mode) and its @media(max-width:480px) align-items flipped from flex-start to center (column/stacked mode) so the logo+badge cluster self-centers while title/subtitle keep text-align:left, unchanged. No transform/position/negative-margin tricks. Google Login section and desktop (>860px) grid layout untouched.
